common_name: Emerald Mist Brunnera (Green-Silver Mottled Siberian Bugloss)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Emerald Mist has softly mottled green-and-silver leaves rather than the fully silvered leaves of some brunnera selections.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade, keeping soil evenly moist through summer since foliage can wilt or scorch in dry conditions or hot sun. Emerald Mist bears heart-shaped leaves softly mottled and misted with silver over a green base, a more subtle, watercolor-like variegation than the boldly silvered leaves of some other brunnera cultivars, giving it a softer, more textural look in the shade border. Airy sprays of small, bright blue, forget-me-not-like flowers appear in early spring above the foliage. Its gentler variegation pairs well with both bold and fine-textured companions, from hostas to ferns to heucheras, without competing for attention the way a fully silver-leaved selection might. Established clumps rarely need division and self-seed only sparingly compared to the plain species.

common_name: Queen of Hearts Brunnera (Bold Silver Heart-Leaved Siberian Bugloss)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Queen of Hearts bears large, bright silver, heart-shaped leaves on a vigorous, quick-to-establish plant.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade, keeping soil evenly moist through summer since foliage can wilt or scorch in dry conditions or hot sun. Queen of Hearts bears large, distinctly heart-shaped leaves covered in bright, reflective silver with a network of fine green veins, on a vigorous plant that establishes and fills in more quickly than some slower-growing silver-leaved brunnera selections. Airy sprays of small, bright blue, forget-me-not-like flowers appear in early spring above the emerging foliage, though the luminous silver leaves remain the main show from spring through fall. Its bright, glowing foliage works well brightening a dark corner of the shade garden and pairs beautifully with hostas, ferns, and hellebores. Established clumps rarely need division and self-seed only sparingly compared to the plain species.

common_name: Cotton Cool Brunnera (Frosted White-Silver Siberian Bugloss)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Cotton Cool has an especially pale, frosty white-silver leaf color, one of the lightest of any brunnera selection.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade, keeping soil evenly moist through summer since foliage can wilt or scorch in dry conditions or hot sun. Cotton Cool bears heart-shaped leaves in an especially pale, frosty white-silver tone with only a thin margin of green remaining, one of the lightest and brightest colored selections in the Brunnera macrophylla group, giving it an almost luminous, cooling presence in a shaded border. Airy sprays of small, bright blue, forget-me-not-like flowers appear in early spring above the emerging foliage. The very pale leaf color provides striking contrast against darker-leaved companions such as purple heucheras, bronze ferns, or deep green hostas. Established clumps rarely need division and self-seed only sparingly compared to the plain species.
